item.title: Jay Alammar：Woke up to this. An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents is #1 in Amazon's AI best s…
item.description:
Woke up to this. An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents is #1 in Amazon's AI best sellers!

@MaartenGr and I wrote it for a simple reason. Agents have already changed how software gets built, and soon how a lot of knowledge work gets done. The group of people who understand them should be far larger than it is today.

We strongly believe that starts with building intuition. And intuition is best delivered with crisp visuals and a sequence of ideas curated so each one prepares the next.

Then comes the code. Once the picture is clear, the code reads like a description of something you already understand. You build agents with LLMs, tools, and memory, not just read about them.

Thank you to everyone who read early drafts, shared it, and picked up a copy. And if you've read it, an honest review on Amazon helps the next reader decide if it's for them.

item.title: Jim Fan：Introducing GR00T 2: our most advanced, open System One model for robotics. It run…
item.description:
Introducing GR00T 2: our most advanced, open System One model for robotics. It runs entirely on your robot’s onboard compute, fully untethered, and you own every weight of it. GR00T 2 features:

1. Long-horizon tasks: dexterous manipulation and whole-body control chained over 20+ steps and 5+ minutes, such as performing chemistry lab experiments or assembling model airplanes end to end.
2. X-Adapt: adapting from easy data sources (human wearables and simulation) and deploying zero-shot to diverse real robots.
3. Unified Cognition: native integrations with frontier agents for advanced physical reasoning, robust error recovery, and safety monitoring.

It's an open-source buffet! We are releasing not only the model weights and X-Adapt recipes (coming December), but also our agentic framework, simulation engine, annotation engine, hardware design, and even training data (100K hours, that's ~11 yrs of experience), all available today!

Everything that moves will be autonomous. Anyone can become a roboticist.

Lock in, build with us!

item.description:
We built Control Room, a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.

It connects every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation, data processing, and more. This works together with our misalignment monitoring systems, and halts model output within 35 seconds of a decision to intervene to stop or pause a job.

Control Room is just one part of our holistic approach for safe frontier model training and deployment.

item.title: Dan Shipper：BREAKING:
item.description:
BREAKING:

@AnthropicAI just dropped Claude Fable 5.2. It’s a paradigm-shifting model if you have a project ambitious enough to give it.

We’ve been testing it at @every, and I’ve seen this crazy explosion of creativity on the team. People are making their own creative software, games for their kids, and documentaries instead of slide decks.

Here’s your day zero vibe check:

• Coding: @kieranklaassen built Everycut, a video editor with the features we use from Premiere, Descript, and other tools—all in one app, with an agent built in. The first version was live in 3 days, and we immediately used it for our internal show-and-tell. This feels like a new era of professionals building their own professional tools, tailored to exactly how they work.

• Games and design: @jackcheng gave it a photo of his toddler’s messy playroom. It turned the actual toys into a playable racing game, with fun details like a stray shoe as an obstacle and a sippy cup as a power-up.

• Knowledge work: @hammer_mt turned his research into a documentary. The model came up with interview questions, he answered them on camera, and it cut the footage together. He called this the most productive 3 weeks of his career.

• A different way of working: Give it a big job and leave it running overnight or over a weekend. But tell it what “done” means: Mike found it could finish the build, then spend another day or two testing. Set the goal, the budget, and how much checking you need before walking away.

• The catch: It’s slow and burns through tokens. Our early-access usage was free, and these projects would have been expensive at API rates. It’s 20% cheaper than Fable 5.1, but for everyday writing, emails, or quick back-and-forth coding, I’d usually reach for something else.

The clearest signal: When our early access ended, @TylerNishida stopped working on some projects until he could get this model back. He didn’t want to build them with anything else.

The best measure of a new model is whether it makes you try things you wouldn’t have tried before.

Fable 5.2 absolutely does that.
